about: Missing Milk Carton is a carton printed with a bold "MISSING" header, an empty white square where a photo would go, and "HAVE YOU SEEN ME?" underneath. It spoofs the missing-person notices that American dairies used to print on milk cartons, but instead of a person, the square holds whatever has quietly vanished from someone's life: motivation, a sock from the laundry, a cancelled show, a friend who left you on read or a promised game sequel that never arrived.
origin: In the 1980s, US dairies printed photos of missing children on milk cartons, which made the carton layout instantly recognizable. A blank version of that design later became a parody template used for anything that seems to have disappeared.
usage:
The only text box sits inside the blank photo square. Name what is missing and, for a stronger joke, add when it was last seen, like a real notice: "my motivation, last seen monday morning".

It works best for things that fade away slowly or that everyone pretends not to notice: a sequel, a refund, a coworker who stopped attending standup, the gym habit from January. A mock-serious tone and a precise "last seen" detail make it land.
ideas: my motivation, last seen monday morning
my left sock, last seen entering the dryer
the refund I was promised in march
my new year's resolution, last seen january 4
the guy who said "I'll fix it after lunch"
